title: Daemon coordination authority adapter
description: Objective: provide the missing production consumer edge for @moe/coordination so typed session/terminal traffic is mediated by real identity, recipient, effect, and durable-store facts rather than test-supplied callbacks. Deliverable: a focused daemon adapter that constructs createCoordinationService/createDurableMailbox over SqliteEventStore, authenticates through committed core session authority, resolves registered recipients/effect-session bindings from durable daemon records, and exposes bounded send/read/ack operations. NOT in scope: MCP framing, free-form chat, remote shell, lifecycle commands, or canary tests. Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.ts/.js, coordination-adapter.test.ts, plus apps/daemon/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml only for the @moe/coordination workspace dependency. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test && pnpm typecheck.
definitionOfDone: The adapter uses real SqliteEventStore and committed session/recipient/effect records; no caller can inject a positive auth, recipient, or terminal-binding answer.
Authenticated addressed REQUEST/RESPONSE/EVENT/CONTROL/HANDOFF messages sequence, replay, and acknowledge durably across adapter recreation, with exact receipt/digest identity.

Forged/expired session, missing capability, unknown recipient, stale cursor, mailbox pressure, and unbound terminal effect each assert the exact @moe/coordination reason code and layer and leave lifecycle authority unchanged.
Advisory text and CONTROL/HANDOFF envelopes can never call a command/lifecycle service; a before/after authoritative-store assertion proves non-mutation.
The @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change; coordination, daemon, and repo gates exit 0 with explicit-path attribution.
taskRails: TDD every behavior change; every refusal test pins the exact stable reason code and refusing layer, and generated sweeps assert a positive case count.
Use only public package roots across package boundaries; no deep imports, test-owned authority, mock-backed acceptance, or optimistic UNKNOWN upgrades.
Keep production files focused, target <=250 physical lines and split before 400; stage and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
READ-ONLY. This is a COMPOSITION task: every piece exists and the work is wiring them without weakening any. Re-measure before naming symbols.

WHAT YOU MUST SUPPLY — packages/coordination/src/coordination-ports.ts defines `CoordinationDependencies` with exactly five members: `authenticate` (CoordinationAuthenticator), `mailbox` (DurableMailbox), `now` (() => number), `resolveEffectBinding` (CoordinationEffectBindingPort), `resolveRecipient` (CoordinationRecipientRegistry).

THE SEAM IS ALREADY CUT FOR TWO OF THEM:
- `resolveRecipient`: apps/daemon/src/coordination/recipient-registry.ts exports `RecipientRegistryService` whose `resolveRecipient` member is ALREADY TYPED `CoordinationRecipientRegistry`. It drops straight in. That registry (task-04e4367, DONE) exists precisely so this adapter never injects a caller-supplied recipient answer.
- `mailbox` and the service: `createDurableMailbox` (packages/coordination/src/index.ts:28) and `createCoordinationService` (:34) are root-published, and apps/daemon/package.json already declares "@moe/coordination": "workspace:*".

THE ACCEPTANCE RULE THAT GOVERNS ALL THREE PORTS, and it is easy to satisfy wrongly: coordination-ports.ts pins the accepted answers to exact key sets — BINDING_KEYS ["capabilities","ok","principalId","sessionId"], RECIPIENT_KEYS ["known","role"], EFFECT_KEYS ["bound","effectId","sessionId"] — and only a FROZEN, EXACT, POSITIVE answer becomes a binding. A thrown, partial, extra-keyed or mutable answer is indistinguishable from no answer at all. So a port that returns correct facts in the wrong shape grants nothing while passing every fact-only assertion.

AUTHENTICATE comes from the durable session authority: SessionAuthorityService exposes `authenticate` (session-authority-contracts.ts:212) and `readActiveSession` (:214). Read both and choose deliberately — DoD 1 forbids a caller-injected positive auth answer, so the adapter must derive it from committed records.

DoD 5 says "the @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change". Check whether it is already declared — it is at HEAD — in which case there may be NO manifest change at all. Say which in your evidence rather than editing to match the sentence.

Record the baseline for all four verification legs: `pnpm --filter @moe/coordination test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`.

So DoD 3's stale cursor is covered by BOTH — the code-bearing ack-regression path asserted as code+layer, and the replay path asserted as exact CURSOR_GAP with exact durableCursor/mailboxSequence values. implementationPlan.note:
GATE ANSWERED: literally (b), structurally insufficient — full evidence posted as task comment comment-cc36ba441ab345768b257a3a95ccbfe4.

Short form. (a) is FALSE: no effect-session binding record source exists under apps/daemon (every effectId hit is a command-decision id, not a terminal binding; runner's effect-kernel carries no sessionId at all; task-6cbff010 which would land it is BLOCKED). (b) is TRUE — recipient-registry-records.ts RecipientRecord.effectId is a committed effectId/sessionId pairing folded by readRecipientFold — but PROVABLY insufficient: resolveRecipient (recipient-registry.ts:230) already tests record.effectId against the address, and checkAddress (coordination-service.ts:80-105) runs it BEFORE the effect port, so any same-fold effect predicate is implied by it, the difference set is empty, and COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID is unreachable. Only unread field is `version`; expiry is already inside readActiveSession on the same clock. Both candidate independent axes are empty.

DECISION: resolveEffectBinding fails closed — typed negative for every query, no positive representable. This satisfies DoD 1 maximally, makes DoD 3's refusal REACHABLE through the recipient guard (register role TERMINAL with effectId, registry answers known:true, effect port refuses, service returns COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID/ADDRESS), and is exactly epic rail 4's rule for absent evidence. Cost stated: effect-wrapper/terminal addresses cannot be served — that surface is out of this task's scope.

DEVIATION DISCLOSED: step 2 says a constant answer is forbidden and (c) means block. Its stated reasoning is that a stub "would pass the happy path and silently grant terminal authority" — a constant NEGATIVE grants nothing and turns an otherwise-vacuous DoD-3 case into a reached one, so the block condition (a safe implementation cannot be verified) does not hold. Rejected alternatives: a registry-derived positive would launder a session's self-declared effectId into terminal authority; an unreachable refusal would leave DoD 3 vacuous.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED. Create apps/daemon/src/coordination/coordination-adapter.test.ts over a REAL SqliteEventStore on a real temp path (mkdtemp under the OS temp root, never inside the repo, removed in an afterEach that runs on failure — this host is win32). Create sessions and recipients ONLY through the production writers (the session authority and the recipient registry), never by hand-crafting rows.

DoD 3 refusal cases, each pinning the exact @moe/coordination reason code AND the refusing layer, and each asserting lifecycle authority is UNCHANGED: forged session, expired session, missing capability, unknown recipient, stale cursor, mailbox pressure, and unbound terminal effect. Seven distinct cases; assert a generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO count.

DoD 2's durability clause is the one most likely to be skipped: sequence, replay and acknowledge ACROSS ADAPTER RECREATION. Close the adapter, rebuild it and the store from the same path, and assert the receipt/digest identity is byte-identical and the cursor resumes. Assert digests by exact equality, never by presence.

DoD 4 is a distinct property, not a variant of DoD 3: advisory text and CONTROL/HANDOFF envelopes can NEVER call a command or lifecycle service. Prove it with a BEFORE/AFTER assertion on the authoritative store — capture its state, drive advisory and CONTROL/HANDOFF traffic, and assert the store is unchanged. "No error was raised" does not prove non-mutation.

TDD RED confirmed: "Cannot find module './coordination-adapter.js' imported from .../coordination-adapter.test.ts", 1 file failed, no tests ran.

Test drives a REAL SqliteEventStore on mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "moe-coordination-adapter-")) — OS temp root, never the repo — torn down in an afterEach that pops every store handle and rmSync's every directory, so it runs on the failure path too (win32 host). Sessions are opened only through adapter.sessions (the production session-authority writer, real Ed25519 proofs) and recipients only through adapter.recipients.register (the production registry writer). No row is hand-crafted.

DoD 2: kinds sweep asserts COORDINATION_ENVELOPE_KINDS.length > 0 AND sent.toHaveLength(COORDINATION_ENVELOPE_KINDS.length) — a sweep that generated nothing fails. Sequences [1,2,3,4,5]; RESPONSE is a real correlated reply against a durable seed REQUEST in the sender's own mailbox. Across recreation (store closed, reopened from the same path, NEW adapter): the read resumes at the durable cursor [4,5], replay from 0 returns all five with digests and messageIds asserted by EXACT ARRAY EQUALITY against the send receipts, and an identical resend returns DEDUPLICATED with identical digest/messageId/sequence/sentAt/expiresAt.

DoD 3, seven distinct refusals, each pinned to code AND layer: forged proof and expired session (COORDINATION_AUTHENTICATION_FAILED/AUTHENTICATION at the coordination layer, plus the DAEMON layer pinned separately through adapter.authenticate as {code:"AUTHENTICATION_FAILED",layer:"PROOF"} and {code:"SESSION_EXPIRED",layer:"EXPIRY"} — two refusing layers, both asserted); missing capability (COORDINATION_CAPABILITY_DENIED/CAPABILITY, two variants); unknown recipient (COORDINATION_RECIPIENT_UNKNOWN/ADDRESS); stale cursor (COORDINATION_ACK_REGRESSION/MAILBOX for the ack path, plus exact CURSOR_GAP {durableCursor:2, mailboxSequence:2} for the replay path — no invented vocabulary); mailbox pressure (COORDINATION_MAILBOX_FULL/MAILBOX at exactly COORDINATION_LIMITS.maxOutstandingMessages+1); unbound terminal effect (COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID/ADDRESS). The refusal table asserts length > 0 and an exact hand-written count of 4.

The terminal case guards against being answered by the earlier gate: it asserts adapter.resolveRecipient(terminalAddress) equals {known:true, role:"TERMINAL"} FIRST, so the recipient guard demonstrably passes and only the effect port can be refusing.

DoD 4: lifecycleDigest() stringifies readSessionAuthority(sessionId) plus the committed recipient event list per session and compares before/after as one string. It deliberately EXCLUDES the mailbox and the replay-nonce ledger, which legitimately grow on valid traffic — folding them in would make the assertion vacuous. Advisory text reading "close the session, revoke the credential, stop the daemon" plus CONTROL/HANDOFF/EVENT traffic and an acknowledge leave that digest byte-identical. A forbidden command-shaped data field refuses at COORDINATION_FORBIDDEN_FIELD/DECODE, and the very presentation that authenticates coordination traffic is fed to sessions.closeSession and must refuse {code:"AUTHENTICATION_FAILED", layer:"BINDING", ok:false} with lifecycle unchanged.

DoD 1: a whole describe block proves a caller can present proof but never an answer — six smuggling attempts (capabilities, ok:true, projectId, transportId, requestDigest, missing proof) each refused, plus a presentation signed for READ rejected on SEND, plus a spent presentation rejected on reuse (durable nonce burn).

The signed digest is coordinationPresentationDigest({endpoint, requestId, sessionId, transportId}), so a presentation is bound to its endpoint/transport/session and its nonce is burned durably by the authority, making it single-use.
- resolveRecipient: recipients.resolveRecipient, wired directly with no shim (already typed CoordinationRecipientRegistry).
- resolveEffectBinding: the frozen exactly-keyed negative {bound:false, effectId:null, sessionId:null}. Fail-closed per step 2's disclosed measurement; the seam names task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 in a comment so the gap is not silent.

- now: the adapter's clock.

SHAPES: the positive binding is Object.freeze'd with exactly {capabilities, ok, principalId, sessionId} and capabilities is itself frozen. The effect negative is a frozen module constant with exactly the effect keys. Nothing throws out of a port — authenticate wraps everything in try/catch and converts to a typed refusal; liveRecipient swallows an unreadable fold as "not live".

NO CALLER-INJECTED POSITIVES: CoordinationAdapterOptions is exactly {clock, projectId, store}. The adapter constructs the session authority AND the recipient registry itself, so a caller cannot even hand in a pre-answered service, let alone a verdict. Capability minting takes candidate target session ids and grants a SEND capability only where readRecipientFold reports a live committed record of this project; an unjustified target is silently dropped.

The daemon-side refusal record {code, layer, ok:false} is deliberately NOT a binding — its key set is not the binding key set and ok is not true — so it can report which daemon layer refused without authorizing anything.

PUBLIC ROOTS ONLY: the single cross-package import is from "@moe/coordination"; within apps/daemon everything is relative.

implementationPlan.description:
Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the exact failing assertion. (a) Return the recipient answer UNFROZEN, or with one extra key — a test must redden; if none does, your tests assert the facts without asserting the shape the contract actually accepts, and the binding would silently never form. (b) Accept a caller-supplied positive auth answer — the forged-session case must redden. (c) Let `resolveEffectBinding` answer positively for an unbound effect — the unbound-terminal-effect case must redden. (d) Let a CONTROL or HANDOFF envelope reach a command service — the before/after store assertion must redden; if it stays green, that test is only checking for an absent error. (e) Break cursor persistence so replay restarts — the across-recreation digest equality must redden. (f) Change only the refusing LAYER on one refusal — a layer assertion must redden independently of the code.

The new files are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` is blind to them — hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after every restore.

comments.content:
STEP-2 GATE MEASUREMENT + a disclosed deviation from the step's letter. Read before QA.

MEASURED, on disk at HEAD 531fb92:

(a) NO dedicated effect-session binding record source exists under apps/daemon.
  - `grep -rn "effectId" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts -l` -> recipient-registry{,-records,.test}.ts, daemon-store-dependencies.ts (`effectId: outcome.decision.decisionId` — a command-decision id), documents/document-work-decision.ts (`effectSha256`/`effectIdentityVersion` — command-effect identity), http/http-contract.ts (`DurableDecision.effectId`, same notion), http fixtures. None is a terminal/effect-to-session binding.
  - `grep -rniE "effect.?binding|EffectSession|sessionEffect|bindEffect" apps/daemon/src packages/*/src` -> only recipient-registry.test.ts and packages/coordination itself.
  - packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-kernel.ts (task-2580a578, DONE) models EffectIntent/EffectClaim/ActivationGrant/EffectResult and carries NO sessionId anywhere; EffectClaim binds wrapperIdentity+lockIdentity, not a coordination session.
  - task-6cbff01023b14b26a78fc5e3eb1dd8a9 "Durable Claude attempt dispatch" is BLOCKED.

(b) TRUE but INSUFFICIENT — and this is the part worth reading. recipient-registry-records.ts does carry an effectId/sessionId pairing: `RecipientRecord { effectId: string|null, generation, projectId, revoked, role, version }`, keyed by `recipientAggregateId(sessionId)`, folded by `readRecipientFold`. So the gate's literal answer is (b). But deriving resolveEffectBinding from that same fold CANNOT satisfy DoD 3:

  PROOF. `resolveRecipient` (recipient-registry.ts:221-238) already checks every field of that record — revoked, projectId, role, and `record.effectId !== wanted.effectId` (:230) — plus activeSession + generation. `checkAddress` (coordination-service.ts:80-105) calls resolveRecipient FIRST and returns COORDINATION_RECIPIENT_UNKNOWN before it ever reaches resolveEffectBinding. So any effect port derived from the same fold is a predicate IMPLIED by resolveRecipient: {recipient known} is a subset of {effect bound}, the difference set is EMPTY, and COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID becomes unreachable. A test naming it would be answered by the earlier guard — the exact defect epic rail 6 exists to stop.
  I checked both candidate independent axes and both are empty: the fold's only field resolveRecipient does not read is `version` (meaningless for binding), and session expiry is already enforced inside readActiveSession via isSessionUsableAt against the authority's own clock (session-authority.ts:371-380), which is the same clock the adapter feeds coordination's `now`.

WHAT I AM DOING, disclosed rather than quiet: resolveEffectBinding FAILS CLOSED. It returns the typed negative for every query, because the daemon holds no committed effect-session binding ledger to attest one. Consequences, all checkable:
  - DoD 1 (no caller-injected positive terminal-binding answer): satisfied maximally — a positive is not representable at all; the adapter takes a store and configuration, never a verdict.
  - DoD 3 (unbound terminal effect refuses with the exact code): REACHABLE, and reached through the recipient guard rather than around it. Register {sessionId S, role TERMINAL, effectId "effect-1"} through the production writer -> resolveRecipient answers {known:true, role:"TERMINAL"} -> the effect port refuses -> COORDINATION_TERMINAL_BINDING_INVALID at layer ADDRESS. The test asserts the registry's positive answer in the same case, so which guard answered is pinned, not assumed.
  - Epic rail 4: this IS the mandated behaviour for absent evidence — unverifiable evidence stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority.
  - Cost, stated plainly: the adapter cannot serve effect-wrapper/terminal addresses at all. That surface (remote shell / terminal) is explicitly out of this task's scope.

WHY NOT report_blocked, which step 2 prescribes for outcome (c): the step's prohibition is "do NOT satisfy resolveEffectBinding with a caller-supplied or constant answer", and its stated reasoning is entirely that a stub "would pass the happy path and silently grant terminal authority". A constant NEGATIVE does the precise opposite — it grants nothing, and it makes the refusal the DoD demands reachable instead of unreachable. Every DoD clause is satisfiable without the missing ledger, so a safe implementation IS verifiable and the block condition does not hold. The alternative readings were both worse: a registry-derived positive would launder a session's SELF-DECLARED effectId into terminal authority (a session registers its own address), and an unreachable refusal would leave DoD 3 vacuous.

WHEN THE LEDGER LANDS: re-point resolveEffectBinding at task-6cbff010's durable attempt/effect-session records. The adapter names that task in a code comment at the seam so the gap is not silent.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
STUBBING resolveEffectBinding IF NO RECORD SOURCE EXISTS — REJECTED, and step 2 makes it a hard gate rather than a judgement call. DoD 1 forbids a caller-injected terminal-binding answer and DoD 3 requires an unbound terminal effect to refuse with an exact code. A stubbed positive would pass the happy path while silently granting terminal authority — precisely the defect this adapter exists to remove. If no durable source exists, reporting blocked with the gap named symbol by symbol is the correct outcome.

A FAKE OR IN-MEMORY STORE IN TESTS — REJECTED by DoD 1, which requires real SqliteEventStore and committed records. A fake proves the adapter agrees with the test's model of persistence rather than the store's, and it cannot exercise DoD 2's across-recreation replay at all.

HAND-CRAFTING SESSION OR RECIPIENT ROWS — REJECTED. Create them through the production writers; the registry exists precisely so recipient answers come from committed records.

WIRING resolveRecipient THROUGH AN ADAPTER SHIM — UNNECESSARY. RecipientRegistryService.resolveRecipient is already typed CoordinationRecipientRegistry, so it composes directly. A shim would add a place for the frozen-exact shape to be lost in translation.

EDITING THE MANIFEST TO SATISFY DoD 5 — REJECTED. The DoD says the @moe/coordination dependency is the only manifest change, but it is ALREADY declared at HEAD. The honest reading is that zero manifest changes may be required; step 6 asks the worker to state which rather than making an edit to match the sentence.

planningNotes.risks:
1. A PORT THAT RETURNS CORRECT FACTS IN THE WRONG SHAPE. The contract accepts only a frozen, exact, positively-keyed record; anything else is silently treated as no answer. The adapter would look right, every fact-only test would pass, and no binding would ever form. Drill (a) targets it and it is the highest-probability defect here.

2. A STUBBED resolveEffectBinding. If the durable record source does not exist, the tempting fix is a constant or caller-supplied answer — which grants terminal authority silently and defeats DoD 1 and DoD 3 together. Step 2 makes blocking the required outcome instead.

3. CALLER-INJECTED POSITIVES GENERALLY. This task exists because the coordination service was previously driven by test-supplied callbacks. Any signature that lets a caller pass in a positive auth, recipient or effect verdict reintroduces exactly that.

4. DoD 4 TESTED AS ABSENCE OF AN ERROR. "Advisory text cannot call a command service" is only proven by a before/after assertion on the authoritative store. A test that checks no exception was thrown passes against an adapter that mutated state successfully.

5. DURABILITY TESTED WITHIN ONE PROCESS. DoD 2 requires sequence/replay/ack ACROSS adapter recreation with exact receipt/digest identity. An in-process reuse proves nothing about the cursor surviving.

6. DEEP IMPORTS. taskRail 2 requires public package roots only; a deep import into packages/coordination/src would work locally and violate the boundary. Step 6 asserts the absence.
